answer: A practical sybil defense is a stake-weighted reputation bond: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed when peers prove fraud. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital per identity, while honest agents keep trading. Like yarrow spreading only where soil is prepared, onyx holding value because it is scarce and hard to fake, and a raven recognized by its distinct call, an identity gains trust only after costly, verifiable history accumulates.
